body:
Refs #4018

## Limits (read first)

- **It closes nothing.** Every forge call is a read, including in the opt-in `--sweep` mode: no issue is closed, labelled, or commented on, and no backlog is read or written. This is the evidence half of issue 4018, not the loop closure the triage also leaves open.
- **A fix that cites the issue number nowhere stays invisible.** If no PR body, branch, or title, no commit message, no GitHub closing reference or Development link, and no caller-supplied `--symbol` names the issue, no check can find it.
- **A passing mention counts as a claim.** An open PR whose body cites an issue number is reported as a claim, even when it only mentions the issue. This errs toward leave-open, never toward close. This PR's own description cites several issue numbers from the original report, so until it merges or closes the helper lists it as a claim on those issues.

## Live proof against kunchenguid/firstmate (2026-09-23, final head, history ref origin/main@9296f9b9, open-PR corpus 1274/1274, every check complete)

| Issue | Known answer measured before this PR | Helper result on the final head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4927 | claimed: PRs 4943 and 4955, maintainer existing-pr stamp | **Reproduced.** claimed by PRs 4943 and 4955 (timeline, corpus, fork branch, stamp, closing keyword) and PR 4026, which an earlier maintainer stamp named and which is still open. |
| 3370 | fixed on main by PR 4656 (commit baede47d), found only by the history check with symbol `rerecord_device` | **Found, now reported more strictly.** `hint: suspected fix to verify: commit baede47d ... (#4656) [history:-S rerecord_device]`. The review required that a caller symbol match never becomes fixed-on-main or a close candidate, because the commit does not cite the issue. The helper therefore surfaces it as a suspected fix for a person to verify, not as fixed-on-main. The verdict line reads claimed only because this PR's own description cites the issue (see the limit above); without that it is open, with the suspected-fix hint. |
| 4412 | partially covered: PR 4775 merged, PR 4832 open | **Reported more strictly.** claimed by PR 4832; merged PR 4775 and its commit 9bc051ff are hints only. That commit says the issue is "related, and not closed by this", so it is not fixing evidence. The earlier partially-covered reading counted a bare mention as a fix, which the review rejected. |
| 4466 | open | **Reproduced.** open, coverage complete. |

The reporter's cases, in one `--sweep`: issues 3966 and 3942 are leave-open, claimed by open PRs 3977 and 3978. Issues 3928 and 3926 have since been closed on the forge, so they are no-action; PR 3944 is recorded as a merged fix for 3926 by its closing keyword, and PR 3946 appears only as a hint on 3928.

## Intent

Upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/4018 (maintainer triage 2026-09-08: ready-for-pr, contract-class opt-in): open issues stay open past the PR or merge that resolves them, so they get handed out again as unclaimed work to whoever samples the list next. The reporter checked ten issues described as queued and unclaimed; eight were dead ends, including one already fixed on main (#3928 by #3946) and several with open fixing PRs that the issue never cross-referenced (#3926 and #3944, #3966 and #3977, #3942 and #3978). Each dead end cost a real check - reading the issue, diffing against main, searching for PRs - before it could be ruled out.

The same failure recurred on 2026-09-23 in this fleet: an issue screen that trusted the ready-for-pr label, and a PR full-text search on bare issue numbers (which GitHub does not index), twice presented already-claimed issues as open. A manual five-check screen then separated them correctly and also found #3370 fixed on main by #4656 while the issue stayed open.

The maintainer's triage constraints for any patch: close or link only with durable evidence (a merged commit, a Fixes reference, or a verified fix on main); leave open issues that still have live helper PRs stamped existing-pr; do not compete with the tasks-axi backlog mechanics; keep forge-owned merge policy out of the command layer's judgment; do not grow into a general issue tracker; never close from title heuristics.

## What Changed

- Add `fm-issue-claim.sh` to screen GitHub issues using timeline and Development links, maintainer stamps, fresh open-PR listings, author fork branches, and local history.
- Provide read-only verdicts and opt-in `--sweep` recommendations that preserve live claims, require fixing evidence for links, and exclude closure candidates when coverage is incomplete.
- Integrate screening into Bearings, document the helper, and add regression fixtures for evidence matching, link lifecycle, pagination, and failed reads.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The read-only change is bounded, and the full review found no new material defects or intent contradictions.

## Testing

The focused executable regression suite, live GitHub screens and sweeps, failure probes, and transcript/API-call checks passed; CLI evidence was saved, while controlled forge-state scenarios passed with stubs but remain untested live.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 7 of 11 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Screen issues with existing PRs: report claims despite ready-for-pr labels, including title-only PR #5376. | ✅ pass | live | Live reported-issue screening; Live title-only claim and main-history fix |
| Sweep issues with live maintainer-stamped helpers: report leave-open. | ✅ pass | live | Live sweep and symbol hints: #3942, #4316, #5349 |
| Screen explicit fixing references on main: identify fixing PRs and commits, while already-closed issues receive no-action. | ✅ pass | live | Live reported-issue screening: #3926; Live title-only claim and main-history fix evidence on issue 4260 |
| Screen incidental references and symbol matches: preserve named hints without promoting them into fixes, links, or closure recommendations. | ✅ pass | live | Live reported-issue screening: #4412, #4482, #4316; Live sweep and symbol hints: #3370 |
| Screen an issue with complete checks and no discovered claim: return open and no-action. | ✅ pass | live | Live sweep and symbol hints: #5415 |
| Supply missing history, a nonexistent issue, or a PR number: return unknown with the cause and exit 1. | ✅ pass | live | Live incomplete-read guards |
| Run batch screens and sweeps: use one fresh corpus per invocation and issue only read operations. | ✅ pass | live | Read-only API call audit |
| Connect or disconnect a Development-sidebar PR: classify the current link and fail closed when resolution fails. | ⏸️ untested | no | No link events appeared in the inspected live candidates, and this phase cannot mutate forge relationships. Provide preprovisioned linked/disconnected issues for live verification. |
| Screen a merged PR whose sole fixing evidence is closingIssuesReferences, including numeric or boolean-looking repository identifiers. | ⏸️ untested | no | No matching live specimen was available. Provide a readable repository with these identifiers and a preprovisioned merged PR linked to its issue. |
| Sweep a still-open issue with fixing evidence: recommend closure only for a default-branch fix with no remaining claim and complete coverage. | ⏸️ untested | no | Discovered explicit main fixes concerned already-closed issues. Reopening issues or creating alternative-base merges is outside this read-only phase; provide preprovisioned specimens. |
| Encounter overlapping PR or issue pages: mark coverage unverified and suppress open verdicts and closure recommendations. | ⏸️ untested | no | Forcing pagination overlap requires controlled concurrent forge writes, which this phase cannot perform. Provide a disposable repository with an authorized concurrent-writer test. |

<summary>🔧 **Review** - 3 issues found → auto-fixed (4) ✅</summary>

- 🚨 `bin/fm-issue-claim.sh:549` - Incidental references become fix verdicts. Commit 9bc051ff explicitly says “Related, and not closed by this: #4412, #4482, #4316”, yet this path records each as merged fix evidence. If an issue’s remaining helper PR is withdrawn, the unrelated commit then produces fixed-on-main and close-candidate. The same inference occurs at bin/fm-issue-claim.sh:412 (timeline references), :516 (branch-matched merged PRs), :560 (any symbol change), :641 (aggregation), :723 (closure recommendation), and :731 (link candidates). Keep these matches as inspectable hints and require fixing evidence before promoting them into resolution recommendations. This narrows deliberately documented behavior, so the remedy needs approval.
- 🚨 `bin/fm-issue-claim.sh:412` - A PR merged into a release or feature branch is classified as fixed-on-main without checking its destination or main ancestry. With no remaining claim, an open issue consequently becomes a close-candidate despite its fix never reaching main.
